metadata.title: Academic Bridge: Foundations for Sovereignty
metadata.notes: Bridging the gap between K-12 and Type 1 Civilization technical tracks.

nodes.title: Mathematics of the Mesh
nodes.description: Linear Algebra and Graph Theory applied to decentralized networks. Understanding eigenvalues in trust-propagation and the geometry of high-dimensional semantic spaces (HDC).

nodes.title: Electrochemistry & Energy Storage
nodes.description: The molecular basis of energy. Oxidation-reduction reactions, electrolyte chemistry, and the thermodynamics of phase-transition in solid-state batteries.

nodes.title: Sovereign Rhetoric & Formal Logic
nodes.description: Critical analysis for a decentralized world. Formal logic, identifying sophistry/propaganda, and the linguistic precision required to draft auditable social contracts.

nodes.title: History of Global Commoning
nodes.description: Case studies in long-term stable cooperation. The Althing, the Haudenosaunee Great Law of Peace, and the Ejidos of Mexico. Patterns of successful decentralized law.

nodes.title: Game Theory for Cooperators
nodes.description: Moving from zero-sum to win-win dynamics. Nash equilibria in peer-to-peer networks, Tit-for-Tat strategies, and the math of 'Sacred Reciprocity'.

edges.rationale: Information theory in the mesh requires foundational graph theory and linear algebra.
Understanding electrolyte chemistry helps troubleshoot advanced battery management systems.
Drafting boundary contracts requires formal logic and rhetorical precision.
Thermodynamic governance is an application of multi-agent cooperative game theory.
